newsitem.title: BOSNIA: First Bosnia presidency meeting starts in Sarajevo.
newsitem.headline: First Bosnia presidency meeting starts in Sarajevo.

text.p: Serb, Croat and Moslem members of Bosnia's newly elected collective presidency met on Monday for the first time at a motel on the outskirts of Sarajevo, officials said.
The presidency chairman, Moslem representative Alija Izetbegovic, was the last to arrive at the "Saraj" motel on the eastern approaches to the Bosnian capital.

Reporters near the motel said Izetbegovic arrived around 4 p.m. (1400 GMT), one hour after the Croat representative, Kresimir Zubak, and 45 minutes after the Serb presidency member Momcilo Krajisnik. It was not imediately clear why he was late.
A spokesman from the office of the international High Representative said each delegation had a separate room, and began their meeting at 4.20 p.m..
The High Representative Carl Bildt and his deputy Michael Steiner attended the start of the talks, but left soon after.

International mediators had struggled for two weeks to broker an agreement over the venue for the first session. Izetbegovic, a Moslem, won most votes in the presidential race and will serve as the body's chairman for a two-year term.
